paragraphs: Acentra Health builds health technology and clinical services for government healthcare programs. Its Medicaid Enterprise System takes in professional, institutional, and dental claims and encounters, whether they arrive by electronic data interchange or on paper.

An automated adjudication engine sends processed claims on for payment and flags the ones that need further review. The rules behind those decisions can be entered without code, so administrators can reflect policy changes and mandates as they arrive. A separate provider management module handles enrollment through a configurable intake application. Before a provider is enrolled, a credentialing service verifies licensing and looks for sanctions. External Quality Review services sit alongside the software.

The company claims more than 30 years of public sector health experience. Its claims platform, it says, has earned CMS certification back to day one of operations with zero CMS findings. The provider module is described as CMS certified and compliant with National Institute of Standards and Technology requirements. A federal claims product is described as carrying an Authority to Operate in secure federal data centers.

quote.text: unites regulatory policies with program specifications on a secure, modular, scalable platform to process billions of claims and payments for participants annually.
